sentences.text: Neophrontops is an extinct genus belonging to the family Accipitridae, specifically within the Old World vulture subfamily Gypaetinae, whose parent group is Aegypiinae.
The type species of this genus is N. americanus, which serves as the primary reference for the group.

All Neophrontops species except N. americanus are known only from fragmentary fossil remains. In contrast, N. americanus is represented by well-preserved fossils from the late Middle to Late Pleistocene deposits of the La Brea Tar Pits in Southern California.

N. dakotensis is known only from a distal humerus dating to the Early-Middle Pliocene, while N. vetustus is known solely from a distal humerus that is morphologically similar to N. dakotensis but approximately half its size.
Although classified with Old World vultures, Neophrontops was native to North America, living from the Burdigalian to the Late Pleistocene, between 18.5 and 0.0117 million years ago.
Six species of Neophrontops have been named, spanning from the Early Miocene to the Late Pleistocene.
Researchers have questioned whether all remains belong to a single species, noting that such a classification would imply an extraordinarily vast existence for one biological species.
